title: Annotatio III §.I close: Luther calls Zwinglians heretics; Zwingli weeps for Wittenberg unity; spiritual presence offered — stop before §.II Bucer/Wittenberg
pass_a_gloss: Indeed he called the Zwinglians Heretics, in Epistle 103 of Buddeus’s Supplement p. 105, writing to Jakob Probst, Licentiate of Theology, among other words: The Zwinglians were most unworthily treated, in that they could not obtain the name of Brothers, but were compelled to depart as heretics, yet so that we might meanwhile have peace by mutual writings, if perhaps God should open their Heart. By this pact Luther was the first Author of the Protestant Schism — all the more untimely, the more studiously the other party sought Concord, Luther himself confessing it, Epistles 98 and 123 in Buddeus, when he writes that Zwingli, openly weeping before the Landgrave and the Estates, begged and broke out into these words: There are no people on earth with whom I would rather be one than with the Wittenbergers, p. 105. And again: that the Zwinglians had promised they were willing to say with the Lutherans that Christ’s Body is truly present in the Supper, but only spiritually, so that we might deign to call them brothers. Ibidem.
pass_b_english: Worse: Luther called the Zwinglians heretics — Epistle 103 in Buddeus’s Supplement, p. 105, to Jakob Probst, Licentiate of Theology: they were treated most unfairly in being denied the name of brothers and forced to leave as heretics, yet so that peace might hold for a time by mutual writings, if God should open their heart.

On that footing Luther became the first author of the Protestant schism — and the more out of season, the more carefully the other side had sought Concord, as Luther himself admits in Epistles 98 and 123 in Buddeus.
He records that Zwingli, weeping openly before the Landgrave and the Estates, begged and cried out: there are no people on earth with whom I would rather be one than with the Wittenbergers (p. 105).
And again: the Zwinglians had promised they would say with the Lutherans that Christ’s body is truly present in the Supper, but only spiritually — if only they might be called brothers. Same place.
source_text: Quin Haereticos Zwinglianos appellavit, in Epistola 103. Buddei Supplementi pag. 105. scribens Jacobo Probstio Theologiae Licentiato, his inter cetera, verbis: Indignissimè affecti sunt Zwingliani, quod Fratrum nomen non potuerunt obtinere, sed pro haereticis discedere cogerentur, tamen sic, ut pacem interim haberemus mutuis scriptis, si fortè Deus illis aperuerit Cor. Hôc pacto Schismatis Protestantici primus Autor, Lutherus; tantò intempestivè magis, quantò studiosius altera pars concordiam quaesivit, ipso fatente Luthero, Epist. 98. & 123. apud Buddeum, quando scribit: Zwinglium palam lacrymantem coram Landgravio & Ordinibus rogasse inque haec verba erupisse: Es seynd keine Leut auff Erden / mit denen ich lieber wolte Eines seyn / dann mit den Wittenbergern pag. 105. Iterumque: Zwinglianos promisisse, se velle cum Lutheranis dicere, Christi Corpus veraciter esse in Coena praesens, sed spiritualiter tantum, ut eos fratres dignaremur appellare. Ibidem.
